newsitem.title: USA: Sealright says may not report 1996 profit.
newsitem.headline: Sealright says may not report 1996 profit.

text.p: Sealright Co Inc said it will close two plants, suspend dividend payments, take an estimated fourth-quarter restructuring charge of $2.3 million and possibly not report a profit for 1996.
In addition, the maker of packaging for dairy, food and beverage products said it will also consider selling an unprofitable line of business later this year.

Shares in the company were down 3/4 to 9-1/2. "Sales slumped during the quarter primarily because of unfavorable market conditions for frozen dairy desserts, some softness in demand from beverage customers, and because of lost business from some small food processors," it said.
The company added that "slow sales kept the company from benefiting fully from its improved operating margins."
Sealright posted a loss in 1995 of $5.7 million, or $0.52 per share, on sales of $294.3 million.

Sealright on Thursday reported earnings for the quarter ended September 30 of $1.7 million, or $0.15 per share, on sales of $68.4 million, versus earnings of $1 million, or $0.09 per share, on sales of $76.2 million a year ago.

"Sealright attributed the earnings increase to substantially improved operating margins resulting from the company's strategic realignment and reorganization, which began in December 1995, and to continued success in cutting selling, general, and administrative expenses," it said.

The company said, "Because of the anticipated $2.3 million in restructuring expenses in the fourth quarter, the company ... may not report a profit for the year ending Dec. 31, exclusive of any charge for the possible sale of the Los Angeles plastics operation."
It added, "If the company were to decide to sell the plastics operation, the loss for the year could range from $0.21 per share to $0.25 per share."
The company said its directors suspended dividends due to the increased restructuring expenses in the fourth quarter and the possible charge for the plastics operation sale.
The company said it intends to resume paying dividends in the future, depending on 1997 performance. --Chicago Newsdesk 312-408-8787
